alex_cheng: Quick question — we need to run a short external probe from a test VM in prod-vpc to a third‑party monitoring IP (35.199.12.8). Probe needs ICMP + TCP/443. Is it OK to add a temporary egress allowlist for that IP? Also: will any request payloads show up in NAT logs? I want to make sure we aren't leaking anything sensitive in logs. Planning window: 2 hours tomorrow.

samira.k: Short answer: allowed with controls, but prefer avoiding ICMP if possible. Policy requires: (1) a ticket in #security-approvals with reason & owner, (2) TTL for the rule (auto-removal), (3) justification for why PrivateLink/VPC endpoint can't be used. NAT logs: only metadata (src/dst IPs, ports, protocol, bytes, timestamps) — no packet payloads.

infra-bot: SECURITY BOT: Please include the following in the approval ticket: project id, requester, start/end times, destination IP(s), ports/protocol, and test plan. Attach the runbook for rollback. See https://intra.redwood/security/egress-policy for template.

jordan_m: If we must do ICMP, ask: can we limit it to a single test VM's ENI? Also, we should add a network ACL entry too so it’s explicit at subnet level (defense in depth).

samira.k: Yes — limit by source ENI and tag the ENI with a ticket ID. Steps I recommend: 1) Create ticket and tag #security-approvals, 2) add egress SG rule allowing 35.199.12.8/32 tcp:443 and icmp-type 8 only from ENI-ID i-0abcxyz, 3) add NACL rule at subnet egress, 4) set TTL 2h and include automated removal hook (we use the cleanup bot), 5) security review sign-off (me or @security on call). Example SG rule snippet you can paste:```
Type: Custom TCP Rule
Protocol: TCP (6)
PortRange: 443
CidrIp: 35.199.12.8/32
Source: sg-allow-test-eni (or ENI tag)
```And for ICMP minimal:```
Type: Custom ICMP
Protocol: ICMP (1)
ICMPType: 8
CidrIp: 35.199.12.8/32
Source: sg-allow-test-eni
```

alex_cheng: Got it — thanks. Two quick follow-ups: (a) Who signs off on the security review if it needs to happen out of hours? (b) Does the cleanup bot need a special label in the ticket to auto-remove?

samira.k: (a) If out of hours, ping @security-oncall and include the ticket link; they can approve for emergency short windows. (b) Yes — include the label `auto-remove:yes` and `cleanup-window:2h` in the ticket body. The cleanup bot will only remove rules that match that label and were created by the requester's service account.

jordan_m: Also note — NAT flow logs are retained in central logs. If you need immediate expiration of logs for this test, we don't support per-entry deletion. Better to avoid sending PII to external monitors.

alex_cheng: Perfect — I’ll open the ticket now and tag you both. Will use TCP only if monitoring supports it, otherwise will request ICMP with strong justification. Thanks :thumbsup:
